messages.irc.help.networks: Your networks, connected ones first, their status, and which one you're on. A filter (lib*, or part of a name) shows only the networks it matches.
messages.irc.help.jumpnetwork: Switch this client to another network.
messages.irc.help.jump: Reconnect to the next server (or the one named); a network name switches to that network.
messages.irc.help.disconnect: Disconnect a network (default: this one). evrd stops reconnecting it.
messages.irc.help.addnetwork: Add a network. +port means TLS (default +6697). With just an id, one from the directory.
messages.irc.help.directory: Public networks you can add by id (addnetwork <id>).
messages.irc.help.delnetwork: Remove a network and its saved history.
messages.irc.help.set: Change a network setting (listed below the table; - clears).
messages.irc.help.listservers: This network's servers, in failover order.
messages.irc.help.addserver: Add a server (tried in turn when the link drops). +port means TLS.
messages.irc.help.listfingerprints: Certificate fingerprints trusted for this network.
messages.irc.help.addfingerprint: Trust a server certificate by its SHA-256 fingerprint.
messages.irc.help.detach: Hide channels from IRC clients; evrd stays in them and keeps logging. /join or attach brings them back.
messages.irc.help.attach: Show detached channels again, with what you missed.
messages.irc.help.disablechan: Leave channels but keep them saved (with their key).
messages.irc.help.channels: The channels saved for this network (JOIN and PART update it).
messages.irc.help.showchan: A channel's state, settings and buffer.
messages.irc.help.buffers: This network's buffers: lines played back, auto-clear, what's waiting.
messages.irc.help.playbuffer: Play a buffer back, as on attach (after its clear mark).
messages.irc.help.playback: Replay a buffer's last lines from history, cleared or not (default 50, up to {max}).
messages.irc.help.clearbuffer: Clear buffers: playback starts after now (history keeps the lines). Wildcards work.
messages.irc.help.clearallbuffers: Clear every buffer on this network.
messages.irc.help.clearallchannelbuffers: Clear every channel buffer on this network.
messages.irc.help.clearallquerybuffers: Clear every query buffer on this network.
messages.irc.help.setbuffer: How many lines a buffer plays back (0–{max}; * for this network's default; - for the default).
messages.irc.help.autoclear: Play back only what's new (on) or the last lines every time (off); - for your account's setting.
messages.irc.help.modules: This network's modules: which are on, and what each does.
messages.irc.help.loadmod: Switch a module on for this network.
messages.irc.help.unloadmod: Switch a module off for this network.
messages.irc.help.modset: Change a module's setting (lines: separate them with " | ").
messages.irc.help.clearbindhost: Back to your account's bind host.
messages.irc.help.showbindhost: This network's and your account's bind hosts.
messages.irc.help.setuserbindhost: Your account's bind host (for networks without their own).
messages.irc.help.info: Your account, limits and attached clients.
messages.irc.help.listclients: Your attached IRC clients and web chats.
messages.irc.help.uptime: How long evrd has been running.
messages.irc.help.traffic: Where to see this network's traffic.
messages.irc.help.listallusernetworks: Admins: every user's networks. A filter (lib*, or part of a name) matches a network's name or its owner's.
messages.irc.usage.addnetwork: Usage: addnetwork <name> <host> [[+]port] [nick] — e.g. addnetwork libera irc.libera.chat +6697 — or addnetwork <id> for a network in the directory
messages.irc.usage.set: Usage: set [network] <setting> <value> — settings: name host port tls nick ident realname password auth …
messages.irc.usage.disablechan: Usage: disablechan <#channel>[,…] — leave a channel but keep it saved (enablechan joins it again)
messages.irc.usage.modset: Usage: modset <module> <setting> <value> (an empty value goes back to the default)
messages.irc.usage.setbindhost: Usage: setbindhost <host> — this network's local address (clearbindhost goes back to your account's)
messages.irc.usage.playbuffer: Usage: playbuffer <channel|nick> — or playback <channel|nick> [lines] for everything saved
messages.irc.usage.setbuffer: Usage: setbuffer <channel|nick|*> [lines|-] — * is this network's default; - goes back to the default
messages.irc.usage.autoclear: Usage: autoclear <channel|nick>[,…] on|off|- — on plays only what's new since a client was last here; - goes back to your account's setting
messages.irc.networks.footerFiltered: {shown} of {networks}. * = this client. jumpnetwork <network> to switch.
messages.irc.disconnect.here: Disconnected from {network}. You're still attached — connect to bring it back.
messages.irc.badPort: {port} isn't a port — use e.g. 6667, or +6697 for TLS.
messages.irc.addnetwork.notInDirectory: No network {id} in the directory — see directory, or addnetwork <name> <host> [[+]port] [nick].
messages.irc.addnetwork.taken: You already have a network called {network}.
messages.irc.addnetwork.added: Added {network} ({host}:{tls}{port}, nick {nick}). connect {network} to bring it online, then jump {network}.
messages.irc.directory.empty: The network directory is empty here (an admin can set it up: network_directory).
messages.irc.directory.noMatch: No network in the directory matches {search}.
messages.irc.delnetwork.current: You're on {network} — jump to another network first.
messages.irc.set.floodrate: floodrate is lines per second, e.g. 2 (0 turns it off).
messages.irc.set.savedReconnecting: Saved {setting} = {value} on {network}. Reconnecting to apply it…
messages.irc.channels.none: No channels on {network} yet. /join one and it's saved.
messages.irc.web.history: The web chat already shows each buffer's history — scroll up.
messages.irc.web.detach: Detaching hides channels from IRC clients; the web chat shows everything.
messages.irc.web.attach: Attaching shows channels to IRC clients; the web chat shows everything.
messages.irc.web.jumpnetwork: In the web app, pick a network from the Networks page instead.

irc.playback.more.one: {count} more line in {buffer} from while you were away: /msg *status playback {buffer} {lines}
irc.playback.more.other: {count} more lines in {buffer} from while you were away: /msg *status playback {buffer} {lines}

messages.irc.info.limits: Networks: {networks} of {maxNetworks}. Clients attached: {clients} of {maxClients}. Backlog: {backlog} lines per buffer.
messages.irc.addserver.done: Added {host}:{port} to {network}. It's used when the link drops.
messages.irc.delserver.last: That's {network}'s only server — add another first.
messages.irc.fingerprints.removed: No longer trusting that certificate on {network}.
messages.irc.modules.footer: loadmod <module> / unloadmod <module> switch one on or off; modset <module> <setting> <value> changes a setting (or use the web app).
messages.irc.modules.switchedOff: An admin has switched {module} off on this server.
messages.irc.module.perform: Commands sent to the server every time evrd signs in: OPER, a MODE, a login to a service the network has.
messages.irc.module.keepnick: When your nick is taken, wins it back as soon as it frees up (and tries every 30 seconds meanwhile).
messages.irc.module.kickrejoin: Rejoins a channel you were kicked from, after a delay.
messages.irc.module.autocycle: When you're left alone in a channel without ops, leaves and rejoins it so you get ops.
messages.irc.module.autoop: Gives ops to the people you list when they join a channel where you have ops.
messages.irc.module.autovoice: Gives voice to the people you list when they join a channel where you have ops.
messages.irc.module.alias: Your own commands for IRC clients: /op #chan nick turned into what you define.
messages.irc.module.ctcpflood: Stops answering CTCP requests (and passing them to clients) while too many arrive at once.
messages.irc.module.q: Logs in to QuakeNet's Q with the network's account and password (under Authentication) instead of NickServ, and hides your host.
messages.irc.chan.disabledLeft: Disabled {channel}: left it, kept it saved. enablechan {channel} joins it again.
messages.irc.traffic.web: Traffic per network is on each network's health page in the web app.
messages.irc.jump.notConnected: {network} isn't connected — connect brings it up.
messages.irc.jump.unknown: {name} is neither one of your networks nor a server of {network} — see networks or listservers.
messages.irc.bindhost.show: This network's bind host: {network} · your account's: {account}
messages.irc.bindhost.userCleared: Cleared your account's bind host. Networks use it when they next connect.
messages.irc.bindhost.userSet: Your account's bind host is {host}. Networks without their own use it when they next connect.
messages.irc.clear.none.channelBuffers: No channel buffer to clear on {network}.
messages.irc.clear.none.queryBuffers: No query buffer to clear on {network}.
messages.irc.clear.done: Cleared {buffers} on {network} — playback starts after now. (History still has them: playback <buffer> or the web chat.)
messages.irc.setbuffer.badLines: Lines is a number from 0 to {max} (or - for the default).
messages.irc.setbuffer.networkSet: Buffers on {network} play back {lines} lines unless they have their own setting.
messages.irc.autoclear.bad: autoclear is on, off or - (your account's setting).
messages.irc.autoclear.on: {buffer} auto-clears: playback is only what's new.
messages.irc.autoclear.off: {buffer} keeps its buffer: playback is its last {lines} lines.
messages.irc.notHere.reloadmod: Modules are built into evrd and always current — nothing to reload.
messages.irc.notHere.updatemod: Modules are built into evrd and always current — nothing to update.
messages.irc.notHere.rehash: evrd applies settings as they're saved; evrd.conf is read at start (restart evrd to re-read it).
messages.irc.notHere.saveconfig: evrd saves every change as it's made.
messages.irc.notHere.restart: Restart evrd from the server (rcctl restart evrd, systemctl restart evrd, or docker compose restart) — the holder keeps everyone connected.
messages.irc.notHere.shutdown: Stop evrd from the server (rcctl stop evrd, systemctl stop evrd, or docker compose stop).
messages.irc.notHere.listports: evrd's ports are in evrd.conf (listen, irc_listen) and on the admin Settings page.
messages.irc.notHere.addport: evrd's ports are in evrd.conf (listen, irc_listen) and on the admin Settings page.
messages.irc.notHere.delport: evrd's ports are in evrd.conf (listen, irc_listen) and on the admin Settings page.
messages.irc.notHere.showmotd: evrd has no message of the day of its own; /motd shows the network's.
messages.irc.notHere.setmotd: evrd has no message of the day of its own.
messages.irc.notHere.addmotd: evrd has no message of the day of its own.
messages.irc.notHere.clearmotd: evrd has no message of the day of its own.
messages.irc.notHere.broadcast: evrd can't broadcast to every user yet.
messages.irc.notHere.movenetwork: Networks can't move between users; add it to the other account instead (the web app's import can copy settings).
messages.irc.err.usernameRules: usernames are 2–32 characters: a–z, 0–9, - and _, starting with a letter
messages.irc.err.passwordControl: passwords can't contain line breaks or control characters
messages.irc.err.bindHostByAdmin: your bind host is set by an admin
messages.irc.err.noBindHosts: this bouncer doesn't offer bind hosts
messages.irc.err.notABindHost: {host} isn't one of this bouncer's bind hosts ({hosts})
messages.irc.err.role: role must be user or admin
messages.irc.err.clientPasswordName: give it a name of up to 64 characters, e.g. the client or device
messages.irc.err.networkLimit: you've reached your limit of {count} networks — remove one first
messages.irc.err.allowedHost: {host} isn't an IP, a CIDR range or a wildcard like 192.168.*
messages.irc.err.networkName: a network needs a name without spaces, / or :
messages.irc.err.altNickChars: the alternate nick can't contain spaces or , * ? ! @ # :
messages.irc.err.identChars: the ident can't contain spaces, @, ! or :
messages.irc.err.floodRate: the flood rate is lines per second, 0–100 (0 turns protection off)
messages.irc.err.quitMsg: the quit message must be one line
messages.irc.err.serverPassword: server passwords must be one line
messages.irc.err.serverNeeded: a network needs a server hostname
messages.irc.err.fingerprint: certificate fingerprints are SHA-256: 64 hex digits (colons optional)
messages.irc.err.channelName: {channel} isn't a channel name — channels start with #
messages.irc.err.channelKey: channel keys can't contain spaces or commas
messages.irc.err.loginMethod: the login method is auto, sasl, nickserv, command or none
messages.irc.err.servicesNick: the services nick is one word, like NickServ or NickServ@services.dal.net
messages.irc.err.identifyArgs: IDENTIFY takes the account and password, just the password, or (empty) whichever fits
messages.irc.err.identifyOn: identify on connect or on prompt
messages.irc.err.ghost: free a taken nick with ghost, regain or recover (or not at all)
messages.irc.err.loginCommandLine: the login command is one line
messages.irc.err.loginCommand: the command login needs a command, like PRIVMSG X@channels.undernet.org :LOGIN %account% %password%
messages.irc.err.encoding: {encoding} isn't an encoding evrd knows (try ISO-8859-1, windows-1252, KOI8-R…)
messages.irc.err.networkTaken: you already have a network called {network}
messages.irc.err.lastAdmin: this is the last admin — make someone else an admin first
messages.irc.welcome.bouncer: Welcome to evrd - a bouncer connection, on no network
messages.irc.bouncerConnection: This is a bouncer connection, on no network: pick one with BOUNCER BIND
messages.irc.hint.banned: The server refuses connections from this bouncer's address. evrd rests that server for half an hour (longer each time, as retrying sooner makes bans longer) and tries the network's other servers meanwhile. Some servers only accept certain countries or networks, or clients with ident; add other servers of the network, or ask its staff why — the server's own words are in the connection log.
messages.irc.hint.throttled: The server limits how often, or how many, connections come from one address — other users of this bouncer on the same network count too. evrd rests that server for at least two minutes, trying the network's other servers meanwhile.
messages.irc.hint.needsLogin: That channel only lets in people logged in to an account. Set up Authentication, and switch on “Join channels after identifying” so evrd joins once services confirm the login.
messages.irc.hint.notRegistered: That account isn't registered on this network. Check the account name under Authentication, or register it first (/msg NickServ REGISTER).
messages.irc.hint.suspended: Services have suspended or frozen this account. Ask the network's staff.
messages.irc.hint.servicesNoAnswer: Services didn't answer the way evrd expected. Check the login method and services nick under Authentication: DALnet's is NickServ@services.dal.net, Undernet logs in to X and QuakeNet to Q (pick their presets).
messages.irc.hint.saslRequired: This server only lets in people who log in with SASL. Set your account and password under Authentication (Automatic or SASL).
messages.irc.hint.hungUp: The server hung up before the secure connection was set up. It may be busy or refusing this address for now, or that port doesn't speak TLS — evrd keeps trying, and other servers of the network may let you in.
messages.irc.hint.noSASL: This network has no SASL. Choose Automatic or NickServ under Authentication, so evrd identifies once connected.
messages.irc.hint.password: The password was refused. Check the account and password under Authentication (and a server password, if the server needs one).
messages.irc.hint.notTLS: This port doesn't speak TLS. Use the server's TLS port (often 6697, sometimes 9999 or 7000), or switch TLS off for this server.
messages.irc.hint.speaksTLS: The server expects TLS on this port. Switch TLS on for this server.
messages.irc.hint.certificate: The server's certificate couldn't be verified. If it's self-signed and you know it's the right server, trust its fingerprint; otherwise check the host name.
messages.irc.hint.noHost: That host name doesn't exist. Check its spelling, or the network's list of servers.
messages.irc.hint.refused: The server's address answered, but nothing listens on that port. Check the port (and that the server is up).
messages.irc.hint.noAnswer: The server didn't answer. It may be down, or a firewall is in the way — of the server, or of this bouncer's outgoing connections.
messages.irc.hint.nick: The nick is taken or not allowed. Set an alternate nick, or another nick, for this network.
messages.irc.hint.pingTimeout: The connection went quiet and was dropped. Usually a network hiccup; evrd reconnects by itself.
messages.irc.hint.closed: The server closed the connection. Its last words, if any, are in the connection log.
messages.irc.reason.hungUp: the server hung up during the TLS handshake
messages.irc.reason.speaksTLS: the server speaks TLS on this port
messages.irc.reason.refusedSASL: the server refused the SASL capability
messages.irc.reason.certHost: it's for a different host name
messages.irc.reason.certNoValidation: certificate validation is off for this network
messages.irc.reason.notTLS: the server didn't answer with TLS on this port — it said {said} (is it a plain-text port?)
messages.irc.log.resumed: Picked up the connection the holder kept while evrd restarted (as {nick})
messages.irc.log.identifyInstead: Will identify to {services} once connected instead
messages.irc.log.noPassword: No password set: not identifying to {services}
messages.irc.log.joinAfterLogin: Joining channels once services confirm the login
messages.irc.log.waitingForPrompt: Waiting for {services} to ask before identifying
messages.irc.log.servicesSilent: Services didn't answer the login within {wait}, so evrd can't tell whether it worked
messages.irc.rest.allBanned: All servers of {network} refuse this address: trying again in {wait}
messages.irc.rest.allLimited: All servers of {network} refuse or limit connections from this address: trying again in {wait}
messages.irc.rest.banned: {host} refuses this address: resting it for {rest}, trying the network's other servers
messages.irc.rest.limited: {host} limits connections from this address: resting it for {rest}, trying the network's other servers
messages.irc.event.linesDropped: {count} lines didn't fit the holder's buffer
messages.irc.event.splitOff: {network}: your server split from the rest of the network
messages.irc.event.splitOffDetail: {lost} of the {of} people in your channels left at once ({reason}). evrd stays connected and counts this time as split off until they come back.
messages.irc.event.rejoined: {network}: your server is back with the rest of the network
messages.irc.module.log.keepnick: keepnick: {nick} is taken; trying for it every 30 seconds
messages.irc.module.log.kickrejoin: kickrejoin: kicked from {channel} by {by}; rejoining in {seconds}s
messages.irc.module.log.autocycle: autocycle: alone in {channel} without ops; cycling it
messages.irc.module.log.ctcpflood: ctcpflood: more than {limit} CTCPs in {window} (latest {command} from {from}); ignoring them
messages.irc.module.log.qLogin: q: logging in to Q as {account}
messages.irc.web.moving: your bouncer is moving to another server — try again in a moment
messages.irc.web.negativeLimits: limits can't be negative (0 means unlimited)
messages.irc.web.deleteSelf: delete your own account from the Account page
messages.irc.web.lockout: that list doesn't include the address you're using now ({address}) — you'd lock yourself out
messages.irc.web.email: that doesn't look like an email address
messages.irc.web.nick: nicks can't contain spaces or , * ? ! @ # : and are at most 30 characters
messages.irc.web.autoAwayDelay: The auto-away delay is 0 to {max} minutes.
messages.irc.web.language: that language isn't one the web app has
messages.irc.web.ssoPassword: your password is managed by your sign-in provider
messages.irc.web.packTooBig: the file is larger than {max} KiB
messages.irc.web.noIRCTexts: no built-in IRC texts for that language
messages.irc.web.packNotJSON: that isn't a language pack: expected JSON like {"code": "de", "name": "Deutsch", "messages": {…}}
messages.irc.web.packCode: {code} isn't a language code: use 2 or 3 lowercase letters, optionally with a region (de, pt-BR)
messages.irc.web.packName: the language's name must be 1 to 40 characters
messages.irc.web.packKey: {key} isn't a message key: use letters, digits, _ . and - (at most 100)
messages.irc.web.packValue: must be text, or plural forms like {"one": "…", "other": "…"}
messages.irc.web.packForm: {form} isn't a plural form: use zero, one, two, few, many or other
messages.irc.web.lines: lines is a number from 0 to {max}
messages.irc.web.autoClear: autoClear is true, false or null
messages.irc.web.autoClearScope: auto-clear is set per buffer (or for the account)
messages.irc.moduleHelp.perform.commands: One per line, as you'd type them in a client: /msg NickServ …, /mode %nick% +x, or raw IRC. %nick% is your nick.
messages.irc.moduleHelp.autocycle.channels: Which channels, one per line; * and ? match anything. Start a line with ! to leave a channel out.
messages.irc.moduleHelp.autoop.users: One per line: a nick!user@host mask, then optionally the channels (comma-separated, wildcards allowed). Example: *!*@friend.example.org #home,#work
messages.irc.moduleHelp.autovoice.users: One per line: a nick!user@host mask, then optionally the channels (comma-separated, wildcards allowed). Example: *!*@friend.example.org #home,#work
messages.irc.moduleHelp.alias.aliases: One per line: name = commands. %1, %2… are the words after it, %1+ the rest from there, %nick% your nick; separate several commands with ;. Example: op = /mode %1 +o %2
messages.irc.settingHelp.irc_host: The host name users point their IRC clients at (shown on the IRC clients page).
messages.irc.settingHelp.public_url: Where the web app is served, e.g. https://bnc.example.org. Single sign-on redirects back here.
messages.irc.settingHelp.max_networks: 0 is unlimited. Admins can override it per user.
messages.irc.settingHelp.backlog_lines: Lines kept per channel or query, pruned every 10 minutes. 0 keeps everything.
messages.irc.settingHelp.connect_rate: The most new connections per second to one server host, per node, so reconnect storms are spread out. 0 is unlimited.
messages.irc.settingHelp.prefer_ipv6: Connect to IRC servers over IPv6 when they have it, and over IPv4 if that fails. Off: IPv4 first. With only IPv4 upstream_bind addresses, IPv4 goes first either way.
messages.irc.settingHelp.client_ping_timeout: evrd pings an IRC client that has said nothing for 90 seconds and drops it when it doesn't answer within this long, so a phone that lost signal doesn't linger. 0 turns it off.
messages.irc.settingHelp.network_directory: Where the list of IRC networks users pick from when adding one comes from: an http(s) URL (checked twice a day) or a file. Empty turns the list off.
messages.irc.settingHelp.tls: For the IRC ports, and for the web app when evrd serves HTTPS itself. Let's Encrypt (acme) gets and renews one automatically, accepting the CA's subscriber agreement.
messages.irc.settingHelp.acme_email: Optional: where the CA writes about expiring certificates or policy changes.
messages.irc.settingHelp.acme_ca: Empty: Let's Encrypt. Their staging directory (https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory) is for trying things out.
messages.irc.settingHelp.tls_cert: PEM, with the chain. Read at startup, before evrd chroots.
messages.irc.settingHelp.password_login: Let users sign in to the web app with a password. Turn off to use single sign-on only (set it up first). IRC clients still attach with client passwords.
messages.irc.settingHelp.session_ttl: How long a web sign-in lasts, e.g. 720h.
messages.irc.settingHelp.cookie_secure: Only send the session cookie over HTTPS. Turn off only for plain-HTTP development.
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_issuer: Your provider's issuer URL, e.g. https://id.example.org/oidc. Empty turns single sign-on off.
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_label: Shown on the sign-in button: “Continue with …”.
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_link_existing: Only if your provider's usernames can be trusted to match evrd's.
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_admin_role: A provider role that makes the user an evrd admin. Empty: admins are set in evrd.
messages.irc.settingHelp.otel_endpoint: Where metrics are sent, e.g. http://victoriametrics:8428/opentelemetry/v1/metrics. Empty turns export off.
messages.irc.settingHelp.metrics_url: VictoriaMetrics' (PromQL) URL the dashboard charts read from.
messages.irc.settingHelp.bindhost: Local addresses (or host names) users may choose to connect from. Space-separated.
messages.irc.settingHelp.acme_hosts: Names the certificate covers. Empty: the public URL's host and the IRC host name.
messages.irc.settingHelp.modules_off: Modules nobody can use on this server (e.g. autoop autovoice), space-separated. Running ones stop at once.
messages.irc.settingHelp.logto_m2m_client_id: A Logto machine-to-machine app with access to the Logto Management API.
messages.irc.settingHelp.logto_m2m_resource: The Management API's indicator. Empty: https://<tenant>.logto.app/api for Logto Cloud, https://default.logto.app/api for a Logto of your own.
messages.irc.settingHelp.sso_irc_password: Lets SSO accounts sign in from IRC clients with their provider password. password_grant asks the OIDC provider (Keycloak, Okta, Auth0, Entra ID…), ldap binds to your directory as the user, logto asks Logto's Management API. Off: SSO accounts use IRC client passwords, which keep working either way.
messages.irc.settingHelp.sso_password_client_id: The OIDC client allowed the password grant. Empty: the sign-in client above.
messages.irc.settingHelp.sso_password_login: What the provider knows the user by: their evrd user name, or their email address.
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_insecure: Send passwords to an ldap:// server without StartTLS. Only on a trusted local network.
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_user_dn: The user's DN, with {username} in it, e.g. uid={username},ou=people,dc=example,dc=org. Empty: search for it (below).
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_bind_dn: Who searches for the user. Empty: an anonymous search.
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_base_dn: Where to search for the user, e.g. ou=people,dc=example,dc=org.
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_user_filter: Finds the user, with {username} in it, e.g. (uid={username}) or (sAMAccountName={username}).
messages.irc.settingHelp.ldap_login: The evrd user name, or the account's SSO subject (when the provider's subject is the directory's user name).
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_roles_claim: The ID-token claim with the user's roles or groups: roles (Logto), groups (authentik), or a dotted path such as realm_access.roles (Keycloak).
messages.irc.settingHelp.oidc_scopes: Scopes to ask for besides openid, profile and email, space-separated. Empty: roles when an admin role is set (what Logto needs).
messages.irc.mfa.noFactor: no authenticator app is set up
messages.irc.mfa.notStarted: start setting up the authenticator app first
messages.irc.mfa.alreadySet: an authenticator app is already set up — remove it first
messages.irc.mfa.needsFactor: set up an authenticator app first
messages.irc.mfa.policyOff: second factors for IRC are turned off on this server
messages.irc.mfa.policyRequired: this server requires a second factor for IRC
messages.irc.web.tooManyAttempts: too many failed attempts — try again in a few minutes
messages.irc.mfa.challenge: A second factor is needed before you're on {network}: /msg {status} otp <code>, with a code from your authenticator app (or a recovery code).
messages.irc.mfa.verifyFirst: Send your second factor first: /msg {status} otp <code>

irc.mfa.wrongCodeTries.one: That code isn't right — {count} try left.
irc.mfa.wrongCodeTries.other: That code isn't right — {count} tries left.

messages.irc.mfa.tooManyTries: Too many wrong codes — sign in again.
messages.irc.mfa.timedOut: No second factor within 2 minutes — sign in again.
messages.irc.settingHelp.irc_mfa: When IRC clients signing in with a password also need a code from an authenticator app: never (off), when the user asks for it (optional), or always (required — users can't turn it off).
messages.irc.settingLabel.irc_mfa_client_password: Second factor with client passwords too
messages.irc.settingHelp.irc_mfa_client_passwords: IRC client passwords are random, per device and revocable, so they don't need a second factor unless this is on.
messages.irc.signin.tooMany: too many sign-in links are open — try again in a few minutes
messages.irc.signin.gone: this link has expired or was already used
messages.irc.signin.notYours: this sign-in is for another account
messages.irc.signin.noSecret: the client didn't send a secret that can be remembered
messages.irc.signin.link: Sign in on the website to connect: {url} (the link works once, for {minutes} minutes).
messages.irc.signin.waiting: Waiting to be allowed on the website: {url}
messages.irc.signin.expired: The sign-in link expired — connect again.
messages.irc.signin.denied: The sign-in was turned away on the website.
messages.irc.signin.otherNode: Allowed — connect again to finish (your bouncer runs on another server of the cluster).
messages.irc.mfa.challengeOrLink: A second factor is needed before you're on {network}: /msg {status} otp <code>, or allow this sign-in on the website: {url}
messages.irc.mfa.linkOnly: Allow this sign-in on the website before you're on {network}: {url}
messages.irc.settingHelp.irc_link_signin: An IRC client without a password it can use gets a link to allow it here, after signing in (with SSO and its MFA). Needs the public URL.
messages.irc.settingHelp.irc_remember_days: Days a device allowed by link and remembered keeps signing in without asking (1–365).
messages.irc.settingHelp.znc_password_days: Days an account made from a ZNC config keeps its ZNC password if no one signs in with it (1–3650). The first sign-in replaces it with evrd's own; unused, it's cleared.
messages.irc.web.importTooBig: that file is too big to import (the most is {max})
messages.irc.web.importUnknown: that isn't an evrd networks file or a ZNC config
messages.irc.web.importNoUser: the file has no ZNC user {user}
messages.irc.netfile.serverPassword: The password for server {host} was saved by another evrd server and can't be read here: set it again.
messages.irc.netfile.loginPassword: The services password was saved by another evrd server and can't be read here: set it again under Authentication.
messages.irc.netfile.loginCommand: The services login command was saved by another evrd server and can't be read here: set it again under Authentication.
messages.irc.netfile.channelKey: The key for {channel} was saved by another evrd server and can't be read here: set it again.
messages.irc.netfile.moduleSettings: The {module} module's settings were saved by another evrd server and can't be read here: set them again under Modules.
messages.irc.netfile.unknownField: {field} isn't a network setting evrd knows, so it was left out.
messages.irc.znc.loginPassword: ZNC's {module} module keeps its password outside the config: set it under Authentication.
messages.irc.znc.moduleData: ZNC's {module} module keeps its settings outside the config: turn it on and fill it in under Modules.
messages.irc.znc.modulesSkipped: evrd has no module for these, so they were left out: {modules}.
messages.irc.znc.passwordUnusable: ZNC's password for this user is in a form evrd can't check, so the account has no password yet: set one, or let them sign in with SSO.
